clue.text: Queen visiting Empire, possibly, for the first night

indicators.note: visiting puts the monarch's letters inside the other piece, as a guest stays within a house
possibly says the word Empire is only one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen calls in on the Empire cinema for an opening night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges EMPIRE to PREMIE, and 'visiting' puts ER inside it, between PREMI and the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: A premiere is the opening performance of a play or film, its debut showing.

clue.text: Lying on arms, can't contain cry of pain

indicators.note: contain says the word for the cry goes inside the letters of the other word

parts.note: can't, dropping its apostrophe, gives the letters CANT
ouch is what you cry when hurt

explanation.surface: Someone lying on their weapons cannot hold back a yelp of pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' here is heraldry (a coat of arms), not weapons; OUCH goes inside CANT, between the C and ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry, a beast drawn lying down with its head raised is described by this term on a coat of arms.

clue.text: Cot made up in back of nuclear plant

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters sit within the word for back

parts.note: the rear is the back of something

indicators.note: made up, as a bed or a story is made up, signals the letters of cot rearranged

explanation.surface: A child's bed is assembled at the rear of an atomic power station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up' turns COT into CTO, which 'in' places inside REAR, after REA.
explanation.definitionFit: A reactor is the vessel where fission takes place, the heart of an atomic power station.

clue.text: Sticking to rules, having some gastric trouble

indicators.note: having some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone keeps strictly to the rules while suffering an upset stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict person adheres rigidly to regulations and allows no exceptions.

clue.text: Twins, for example, reversing small car

indicators.note: reversing, as a car backs up, says the letters for 'for example' are read backwards

parts.note: e.g., exempli gratia, is the abbreviation for 'for example'
the Mini is a classic small British car

explanation.surface: Two siblings back a little motor out of a parking space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns EG into GE, followed by MINI.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini is the zodiac sign of the twins Castor and Pollux.

clue.text: First bogeyman, say?

parts.note: bogey is old slang for a policeman, so the first bogeyman is the statesman who founded the Metropolitan Police, whose name gave police officers the nickname bobby

explanation.walkthrough: A bogeyman is usually a monster that frightens children, but 'bogey' was slang for a policeman, so the 'first' one is the Home Secretary who created London's police force in 1829.
explanation.definitionFit: This British prime minister set up the Metropolitan Police, so he is in effect the founder of the modern constabulary.

clue.text: Photographing dense undergrowth from estate-car

parts.note: shooting a film or picture is photographing it
a brake is a thicket of dense bushes or bracken

explanation.surface: Someone takes pictures of thick shrubbery from the back of a family car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word here: wordplay from definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An old term for a station wagon, originally a vehicle built to carry a hunting party and its guns.

clue.text: Sinister control in Rome, possibly?

parts.note: sinister is Latin for left, and control here means driving a car with its steering on that side, as cars in Italy have

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinister' looks like menace but is the Latin for left; Italians drive on the right, so their cars put the steering wheel on the left.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a vehicle whose steering wheel is on the left, as in countries driving on the right such as Italy.

clue.text: Acid to assist blind farmhouse victims

definitions.note: the answer is the adjective naming a type of acid, as in the acid found in ants

parts.note: to be for someone is to support or assist them

indicators.note: the farmer's wife cut off the tails of the blind trio in the rhyme, so as her victims they lose their last letter

parts.note: blind brings to mind the three blind mice of the nursery rhyme

explanation.surface: An acid is used to help sightless animals hurt on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'Three Blind Mice' the farmer's wife cuts off their tails with a carving knife, so the victims are MICE with the tail docked: MIC, after FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Formic acid is the stinging compound found in ants, whose Latin name formica gives the word.

clue.text: Fifi acts to reform base, cowardly fellows (once)

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters of fifi acts are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman called Fifi behaves in a way meant to improve lowly, timid men.
explanation.walkthrough: '(once)' marks the definition as an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Caitiff is an archaic word for a despicable coward, a mean wretch.

clue.text: Henry to retire? That's new!

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the word to is read backwards

explanation.surface: A man named Henry is about to retire, and someone exclaims at the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retire' reverses TO to OT after H.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot news is fresh and just in, as in hot off the press.

clue.text: Goddess armed from the outset, at that time, in two acres

indicators.note: in says the time word is put inside the pair of letters for the acres

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for acre, so two acres give two As
then means at that time

explanation.surface: A goddess, armed from the start, stands then within a couple of acres.
explanation.walkthrough: THEN goes between the two As. In myth the goddess sprang fully armed from the head of Zeus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess of wisdom and war was born in full armour from her father's head.

clue.text: Flat old hat? Correct!

parts.note: old hat means unfashionable, which is out
right means correct

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a squashed old hat is the right description, and is told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' is not level ground but flat as in a flat refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat denial is a total, unqualified one, so the two words are synonyms meaning absolute.

clue.text: Single game point

definitions.meaning: in cricket a single is one scored between the wickets
in cricket or baseball the unit of scoring is the point gained by completing a circuit or dash

explanation.definitionFit: A cricket single is one such score, and it is the basic scoring unit in baseball and cricket games.

clue.text: Detailed popular measure

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
depth is a measurement, how deep something is

explanation.surface: A detailed report concerns a popular yardstick.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-depth study is thorough and comprehensive.

clue.text: Standard power on a river

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Ordinary electricity is generated on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word joining P to A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the normal or expected level, the benchmark.

clue.text: School of minor surgery

definitions.meaning: ... College is an English independent school in West Sussex
piercing a boil with a small blade is a minor surgical act

explanation.definitionFit: The name of a private school in Sussex and the act of piercing a boil with a small blade.

clue.text: A jolly college, we hear, of heraldry

parts.note: Jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

indicators.note: we hear says the college's name is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: Oriel is a college of Oxford University

explanation.surface: A cheerful college is said to be the one dealing with heraldry.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'jolly' is slang for a Royal Marine (RM); ORIEL, an Oxford college, sounds like ORIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Armorial means relating to coats of arms, the subject of heraldic study.

clue.text: Muse, a variety of lilac almost in bloom

indicators.note: a variety of says the letters of lilac appear in a different form
almost says the last letter of the flowering word is dropped

parts.note: a flower in bloom is open

explanation.surface: A Muse is a variety of lilac nearly in flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a variety of' rearranges LILAC to CALLI; 'almost' trims OPEN to OPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Calliope is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, the one for epic poetry.

clue.text: Filter out quarter of what is fruit-bearing

indicators.note: out, as in out of order, says the letters of filter are disordered

parts.note: E for east is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Sieve out a quarter of what produces fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges FILTER to FERTIL; E is east, one of the compass quarters. 'of what is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fertile land is productive, yielding crops and fruit abundantly.

clue.text: Not easily moved over bad route

indicators.note: over, as in turned over, signals that the letters of bad route are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stubborn will not be shifted from a poor road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' tempts as the anagram signal, but ROUTE alone is too short; the whole of BAD ROUTE is the fodder and 'over' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: An obdurate person is stubborn and unyielding, unmoved by persuasion.

clue.text: Liquid lost in purposeful lager production

indicators.note: in says the answer lies inside the words that follow, across the end of one and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Some liquid goes to waste during determined beer brewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' completes the surface; the answer sits across purposeFUL LAGEr.
explanation.definitionFit: Ullage is the amount by which a cask falls short of full, through leakage or evaporation.

clue.text: Nettles in sausages with head cut off

indicators.note: with head cut off says the first letter of the word for sausages is removed

parts.note: bangers is British slang for sausages

explanation.surface: Stinging plants are found in sausages whose ends have been chopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nettles' is a verb here, meaning irritates; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To nettle someone is to irritate them, a verb sense of the same meaning.

clue.text: Complaint of youth in springtime

indicators.note: in says the youth is placed inside the month

parts.note: May is a month of spring
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A young man has a grievance in the spring.
explanation.walkthrough: LAD goes inside MAY, between MA and Y; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an illness or ailment.

clue.text: Greek character met in your holidays

indicators.note: met in says the answer is found inside the words that follow, spanning two of them

explanation.surface: Someone from Greece was encountered on your vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across yoUR HOlidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Rho is the seventeenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Georgia's airy source of Victorian brilliance?

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia, plus the possessive S
light means airy, not heavy

explanation.surface: Georgia's breezy lamp lit up the nineteenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamps burning coal gas lit Victorian streets and homes.

clue.text: Dried fruit is getting wet

indicators.note: getting means the wet weather takes in the word is, holding it inside

parts.note: the wet is rainy weather, rain

explanation.surface: Dried fruit is getting soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: IS goes inside RAIN, between RA and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape.

clue.text: Glad aeroplane is refurbished for writer of stories

indicators.note: refurbished, as an aircraft is rebuilt, signals the letters of glad aeroplane rearranged

explanation.surface: A happy pilot's plane is renovated for an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' and 'for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The American author of macabre tales such as The Tell-Tale Heart.
